verification_methodology_note: PRIMARY SOURCE ACCESS: laws.boe.gov.sa's LIVE portal was unreachable this pass (direct HTTPS connection attempts to both the specific law-detail URL and the BOE domain root returned curl exit code 35 / empty response, repeated across multiple attempts). HOWEVER, a Wayback Machine snapshot of this exact BOE law page (archive.org/wayback/available confirmed a snapshot timestamped 20251116121007, re-queried at timestamp=20260717 and confirmed still the closest available snapshot -- i.e. no newer BOE snapshot exists) WAS reachable and is treated as this track's PRIMARY source. Unlike this corpus's cooperative_health_insurance_law track (where https:// failed and only http:// worked for the Wayback fetch), for THIS law https://web.archive.org/ succeeded directly (HTTP 200, ~94KB) while http:// returned HTTP 403 -- both schemes were tried per this corpus's established practice, and whichever worked was used; no hostname tricks or bypass beyond the two established proxies were used. The page was parsed with BeautifulSoup (not naive regex/tag-stripping) locating each 'article_item' div and its 'HTMLContainer' child, recovering the complete, correctly-structured text of all 44 articles including nested (أ/ب/ج...، 1/2/3...) list structures, the decree number/date, the full preamble of both the Royal Decree (M/59, 4/11/1426H) and its underlying Council of Ministers Resolution No. 276 (3/11/1426H), and BOE's own per-article HTML class attributes -- all 44 'article_item' divs carry ONLY the class 'no_alternate' (BOE's no-op/default marker), with zero occurrences of any amended/repealed marker class and zero occurrences of the literal words 'معدلة' or 'ملغية' anywhere near an article body (the only two occurrences of those words on the whole page are the page's own generic filter-checkbox UI labels 'مادة معدلة' / 'مادة ملغية', which are unrelated to any specific article). This is corroborated by BOE's page-level 'الحالة' (status) field reading 'ساري' (in force) with no separate historical-version indicator. SECONDARY CROSS-VERIFICATION: nezams.com (fetched live, directly, with a standard browser User-Agent header) provided an independent HTML transcription of all 44 articles, plus its own dedicated 'التعديلات' (amendments) metadata field which states in so many words: 'لم يجرِ عليه تعديل' (no amendment has been made to it). A full normalized text comparison (diacritic-insensitive, alef/yeh/teh-marbuta-normalized, dash-normalized) of all 44 articles between the BOE-via-Wayback text and the nezams.com text found substantive agreement on 42 of 44 articles with ZERO differences, and two trivial, individually-identified discrepancies confined to nezams.com's own transcription (see known_unresolved_discrepancies for both -- neither affects this track's adopted text, which follows BOE in both cases). STRUCTURAL CROSS-VERIFICATION (chapter/فصل/فرع structure): BOE's own per-article HTML/text view does NOT render any فصل (chapter) or فرع (section) heading elements inline with the articles (grep of the raw fetched HTML for 'فصل' or 'الباب' returns zero true matches), but BOE's OWN 'نبذة عن النظام' (about-the-law) summary field on the same page describes the law in exactly five ordered topical groups matching a 5-chapter structure (license to practice; practitioner duties, itself subdivided into general duties / duties toward patients / collegial duties; professional liability, subdivided into civil / criminal / disciplinary liability; investigation and trial; and closing provisions). This structure was then independently confirmed, with explicit 'الفصل الأول' through 'الفصل الخامس' and 'الفرع الأول' through 'الفرع الثالث' headers plus exact per-article boundaries, by moh.gov.sa's own official consolidated Arabic PDF (Law + Implementing Regulation combined, https://www.moh.gov.sa/Ministry/Rules/Documents/Executive-Regulations-Health-Profession-1.pdf) and cross-checked once more against moh.gov.sa's official English-translation PDF of the same consolidated document (https://www.moh.gov.sa/en/Ministry/Rules/Documents/Law-of-Practicing-Healthcare-Professions.pdf), whose 'Chapter (1)' through 'Chapter (5)' / 'Section (1)' through 'Section (3)' markers align exactly, article-for-article, with the Arabic PDF's فصل/فرع markers. All three independent renderings (BOE prose summary, MOH Arabic consolidated PDF, MOH English consolidated PDF) agree precisely on the same five chapters, the same three-way subdivision of Chapters 2 and 3 into فرع/Section groups, and the same article-number boundaries for every division -- this track's chapter_structure field reflects that structure. Chapters 1, 4 and 5 have no فرع subdivisions. AMENDMENT STATUS: this Royal Decree (M/59, 4/11/1426H) itself has NEVER been amended since enactment, per BOE (zero per-article amendment markers) and nezams.com (explicit 'لم يجرِ عليه تعديل' statement) alike -- all 44 articles are recorded as اصلية (original). A pending PROPOSED amendment (Shura Council approval, reported in Arabic press in December 2023, to add a new Article 4 bis / 'المادة الرابعة مكرر' authorizing the Ministry to license independent individual Saudi health practitioners in home-health specialties) was located via multiple Arabic news sources but has NOT been enacted via Royal Decree as of this pass -- see known_unresolved_discrepancies; its proposed text is documented there for transparency but is NOT added as an article in this track, consistent with this corpus's zero-fabrication rule. SUPERSESSION: Article 42 of the Law itself expressly repeals (a) the Law of Practicing Medicine and Dentistry Professions (نظام مزاولة مهنة الطب البشري وطب الأسنان), Royal Decree No. M/3 dated 21/2/1409H, and (b) the Law of Practicing Pharmacy and Trading in Medicines and Medical Preparations (نظام مزاولة مهنة الصيدلة والاتجار بالأدوية والمستحضرات الطبية), Royal Decree No. M/18 dated 18/3/1398H -- both confirmed superseded, matching this corpus's own coverage-gap-map estimate exactly. COMPANION IMPLEMENTING REGULATION: confirmed to exist -- Ministerial Resolution No. 4080489 dated 2/1/1439H (per both nezams.com's 'الملحقات' field and the MOH consolidated PDF's own title page), issued pursuant to Article 43 of this Law. Consistent with this corpus's established precedent (banking_control_law, insurance_control_law, finance_companies_law, cooperative_health_insurance_law), this track ingests ONLY the primary 44-article Law; the Implementing Regulation is flagged as a follow-up candidate, not fabricated or partially guessed at. No legal text is altered. Arabic governs; no translation/paraphrase/interpretation. Read-only over input; deterministic over outputs.

known_unresolved_discrepancies.description: Article 36 (المادة السادسة والثلاثون) refers to '(الهيئة الصحية الشرعية)' -- the 'Sharia Medical/Health Legal Panel' created in Article 33 and referenced identically in Articles 27, 33, 34 and 35 throughout the Law. BOE-via-Wayback uses 'الشرعية' consistently in all five occurrences (Articles 27, 33, 34, 35, 36). nezams.com's independent transcription ALSO uses 'الشرعية' consistently in four of those five occurrences (27, 33, 34, 35) but has an isolated single-character typo in its transcription of Article 36 specifically -- 'الشريعية' (with an extra ي) -- inconsistent with its own parallel usage everywhere else in the same document. This track adopts BOE's 'الشرعية' for Article 36, both because it is BOE's own primary-source text and because it is the internally consistent spelling used by nezams.com itself in every other occurrence of the same defined term.

Article 44 (المادة الرابعة والأربعون), the Law's final and shortest article, is immediately followed on nezams.com's page by that site's own navigation/footer text ('عرض كل المواد' / 'عن الموقع' / 'اتصل بنا' -- 'show all articles' / 'about the site' / 'contact us'), which a naive scrape (with no following article header to bound it) would otherwise append to Article 44's text. This is a page-boundary scraping artifact on nezams.com's site layout, not a discrepancy in the legal text itself -- BOE's text for Article 44 is unambiguous, self-contained, and was used as-is; the site-navigation fragment was excluded during extraction and is documented here only for full transparency of the verification process.

Multiple independent Arabic news sources (Al-Riyadh, Okaz, Makkah, Mubasher, Maaal -- December 2023) report that the Shura Council (مجلس الشورى) approved a PROPOSAL to add a new 'المادة الرابعة مكرر' (Article 4 bis) to this Law, reading: 'على الوزارة تنظيم منح الممارس الصحي السعودي الفرد المستقل في التخصصات المناسبة ترخيصاً بممارسة تخصصه، وتحدد اللائحة التنفيذية التخصصات المناسبة والشروط والضوابط اللازمة لذلك' (authorizing the Ministry to regulate licensing of independent individual Saudi health practitioners in appropriate specialties, e.g. home-health services), aimed at regulatory coordination with Vision 2030 gig/independent-work objectives. Shura Council approval is only one step in the Saudi legislative process (Council of Ministers endorsement and a Royal Decree are still required to enact a Basic-Law amendment into force). As of this pass -- BOE's own Wayback snapshot (dated 2025-11-16, re-confirmed as still the closest available snapshot when re-queried at timestamp 2026-07-17) and nezams.com's live page (fetched today, whose own 'التعديلات' field explicitly states 'لم يجرِ عليه تعديل' -- no amendment has been made) -- neither primary nor secondary source shows this proposed article as enacted. This track therefore documents the proposal's existence and exact proposed wording here for transparency but does NOT add it as an in-force article (no healthcare_professions_art_004_mukarrar record), consistent with this corpus's zero-fabrication rule. This is a candidate to re-check in a future pass in case a Royal Decree has since been issued.

The Law's companion Implementing Regulation (اللائحة التنفيذية لنظام مزاولة المهن الصحية) is confirmed to exist -- issued by Ministerial Resolution No. 4080489 dated 2/1/1439H pursuant to Article 43 of the Law -- and is hosted, consolidated together with the primary Law's own text article-by-article, on moh.gov.sa (both an Arabic PDF and an official English-translation PDF, each labeled 'الإصدار الثالث' / 'Third Edition', 1440H/2019, suggesting at least two prior consolidated-booklet reprints of the Regulation -- an edition/printing label on MOH's own compiled booklet, not a re-enactment of the primary Law itself, which BOE and nezams.com both confirm remains unamended since 1426H). Consistent with this corpus's established precedent for banking_control_law, insurance_control_law, finance_companies_law and cooperative_health_insurance_law (each of which identified but did not ingest its companion Implementing Regulation in the same pass as the primary Law), this track ingests ONLY the primary 44-article Law. The Implementing Regulation -- including its own chapter-by-chapter provisions (referenced in this track's chapter_structure notes only insofar as BOE's own summary describes the primary Law's structure) -- is documented here as a candidate for a dedicated follow-up ingestion pass, not fabricated or partially guessed at.
